instructions: Ten real stories: seven from the 2026-11-03 gpt-5.6-terra run (gpt_judge holds that run's judge), three from a 2026-11-17 local qwen3:14b run. Rate `human` 1-5 blind, before reading any judge score, using the judge rubric: 1 unusable, 3 needs edits, 4 ready, 5 excellent; penalize invented requirements. `judge` is then filled by the current eval judge. Approved rows are copied into calibration.json.

scores.gpt_judge_rationale: The story is focused, valuable, and small, with clear actor, outcome, and two testable single-value filtering scenarios. It aligns with REQ-003 and does not add unsupported scope. Minor edits would make it fully test-ready: define what counts as an actor identifier (format/canonical matching) and clarify expected behavior for no matching records, invalid/empty values, and clearing the filter.

story.title: Filter Audit History by Actor Identifier
story.i_want: to filter audit history by a single actor identifier value
story.so_that: I can view audit records associated with that actor
acceptance_criteria: Given an administrator is viewing audit history, when the administrator applies a filter with one actor identifier value, then the audit history displays only records associated with that actor identifier.

Given an administrator has applied an actor identifier filter, when the administrator changes the filter to a different single actor identifier value, then the audit history displays only records associated with the newly specified actor identifier.

requirements.text: Allow administrators to filter audit history by a single actor identifier value.
requirements.quote: Allow administrators to filter audit history by actor identifier.
requirements.speaker: Eli (administrator)
requirements.note: HD-AUDIT provides record-specific audit history but states that the baseline does not include a general actor filter, so this administrator actor-filter capability is additional scope.

scores.judge_rationale: The story is well-structured with clear roles, intentions, and acceptance criteria. It includes a requirement reference and context from the requirements document. However, it could be improved by adding negative test cases (e.g., invalid actor identifiers) and edge cases (e.g., no matching records). No invented requirements are present.

scores.gpt_judge_rationale: The story is independent, valuable, small, and directly traceable to REQ-002. Its acceptance criteria are clear and testable for revocation and continued non-acceptability before expiry. It correctly avoids inventing details such as authorization rules, UI behavior, or account-creation handling (the latter belongs to REQ-003). A minor edit would clarify whether revocation is allowed only while unexpired and define the expected outcome if a coordinator attempts to revoke an already expired invitation.

story.title: Revoke an unexpired invitation
story.i_want: to revoke an invitation before it expires
story.so_that: the invitation can no longer be accepted
acceptance_criteria: Given an invitation is unexpired, When a coordinator revokes it, Then the invitation is recorded as revoked.
Given an invitation is revoked, When its expiration time has not yet passed, Then it remains unavailable for acceptance.

requirements.text: The product must allow a coordinator to revoke an invitation before it expires.
requirements.quote: Allow a coordinator to revoke an invitation before it expires.
requirements.speaker: Owen (coordinator)
requirements.note: Manual revocation of an unexpired invitation is explicitly not specified in the baseline and is identified as a potential future feature.

scores.judge_rationale: The story is partially testable but lacks sufficient detail for full implementation. The acceptance criteria are clear but could be expanded to include edge cases (e.g., what happens if the invitation is already accepted, or if the revocation is attempted after expiration). The requirement also notes that this feature is not in the baseline and may be a future feature, which introduces uncertainty about its priority and scope.

scores.gpt_judge_rationale: The story is focused and INVEST-aligned: it covers one clear revoked-invitation outcome for a defined user, has direct value, and is small and testable. Both acceptance criteria are deterministic and map exactly to REQ-003: rejection with a revoked explanation and no account creation. It does not invent requirements; the prerequisite ability to revoke is separately covered by REQ-002.

story.title: Reject acceptance of a revoked invitation
story.i_want: to receive an explanation when I try to accept a revoked invitation
story.so_that: I know why I cannot complete account creation
acceptance_criteria: Given an invitation has been revoked, When an invitee attempts to accept it, Then the product rejects the acceptance and explains that the invitation was revoked.
Given an invitation has been revoked, When an invitee attempts to accept it, Then the product does not create an account.

requirements.text: The product must reject acceptance of a revoked invitation, explain that it was revoked, and must not create an account.
requirements.quote: Reject it and explain that it was revoked. It must not create an account.
requirements.speaker: Owen (coordinator)
requirements.note: The invitation workflow defines handling for valid, expired, and used invitations but does not define revoked invitations or their acceptance response.

scores.judge_rationale: The story is well-structured with clear roles, goals, and acceptance criteria. The criteria are testable and cover both the rejection explanation and the prevention of account creation. The requirements are aligned and not overly invented. However, there is a small gap in the story's completeness (e.g., no mention of error messages or UI feedback beyond the explanation), which could be improved for full clarity.

scores.gpt_judge_rationale: The story is valuable and mostly testable: it identifies the member, item, interval, email channel, and portal-link content. However, it omits required related behavior: members must be able to unsubscribe (REQ-006), and it does not state that a notification does not create a reservation (REQ-005). More importantly, subscription expiry is explicitly undecided (REQ-007), leaving lifecycle behavior ambiguous. The criteria should also define what qualifies as availability within an interval and expected behavior for duplicate subscriptions or repeated availability events. No unsupported requirements should be added; the expiry rule needs stakeholder clarification.

story.title: Subscribe to item availability notifications
story.i_want: to subscribe to an email notification for a selected item and date interval
story.so_that: I am notified when that item becomes available during the interval I need
acceptance_criteria: Given I am viewing a selected item, when I provide a date interval and submit an availability-notification subscription, then the system records my subscription for that item and date interval.

Given I have an active availability-notification subscription for an item and date interval, when the item becomes available in that interval, then the system sends an email notification to me containing a portal link.

requirements.text: The system must allow members to subscribe for an email notification when a selected item and date interval becomes available.
requirements.quote: Let members subscribe to an email when a selected item and date interval become available.
requirements.speaker: Jun (member representative)
requirements.note: HD-BOOKING excludes subscriptions to newly available slots and HD-NOTIFY excludes waitlist notifications from the baseline.

requirements.text: Availability notifications must be sent by email and include a portal link.
requirements.quote: Send an email with a portal link.
requirements.speaker: Jun (member representative)
requirements.note: HD-NOTIFY defines email and portal links for existing reservation notifications, but not for availability notifications.

scores.judge_rationale: The story is well-structured with clear acceptance criteria and links to requirements. It includes sufficient context for testing and covers both subscription and notification aspects. However, some requirements (e.g., HD-BOOKING and HD-NOTIFY) are referenced but not fully defined in the provided data, which may affect testability if those specs are not available.

scores.gpt_judge_rationale: Focused, independent story with clear member value and two testable criteria: unsubscribing disables the subscription, and inactive subscriptions generate no availability email. It aligns with REQ-006 without expanding scope. Minor edits: “marks ... inactive” assumes a particular internal state rather than specifying observable opt-out behavior, and the story does not state that a member may unsubscribe only their own subscription. These are small clarifications, not blockers.

story.title: Unsubscribe from availability notifications
story.so_that: I no longer receive availability emails I do not want
acceptance_criteria: Given I have an active availability-notification subscription, when I unsubscribe from it, then the system marks the subscription as inactive.

Given an availability-notification subscription is inactive, when its selected item becomes available during its date interval, then the system does not send an availability email for that subscription.

requirements.text: Members must be able to unsubscribe from availability notifications.
requirements.quote: Yes, members must be able to unsubscribe.
requirements.speaker: Jun (member representative)
requirements.note: HD-NOTIFY requires opt-out behavior to be identified for any new notification, but does not specify an unsubscribe mechanism for availability notices.

scores.judge_rationale: The story has clear acceptance criteria that are testable and specific. It includes a reference to a requirement, and the requirement itself is well-defined. However, it could be improved by adding more context or scenarios (e.g., what happens if a user tries to unsubscribe multiple times, or if the subscription is already inactive). No invented requirements are present.

scores.gpt_judge_rationale: The story is valuable, small, and mostly testable: the criteria clearly cover availability visibility, exclusion of reservation/member data, and read-only behavior. However, it depends on a public status page whose creation is only stated in REQ-001, while the story traces only to REQ-002; REQ-001 is marked as conflicting with the baseline. The acceptance criteria also need a defined availability indicator/source and clearer verification scope for “no action” (for example, no state-changing UI controls or public API operations). Resolve the public-page conflict and link/clarify the enabling requirement before implementation.

story.title: Restrict public status page content
story.i_want: to view service availability on the public status page without access to cooperative data or change actions
story.so_that: I can check service status without exposing protected information or modifying the system
acceptance_criteria: Given a public visitor opens the status page, When the page is displayed, Then it shows service availability.
Given a public visitor opens the status page, When the page is displayed, Then it does not show reservation data or member details.
Given a public visitor opens the status page, When the page is displayed, Then it provides no action that changes system data or state.

requirements.text: The public status page must show service availability only and must not expose reservation data, member details, or any action that changes anything.
requirements.quote: No. Show service availability only, without reservation data, member details or an action to change anything.
requirements.speaker: Eli (administrator)
requirements.note: Although the access rules limit anonymous visitors to sign-in and a generic cooperative description, they do not specify a public status page with these restricted contents.

scores.judge_rationale: The story is well-structured with clear roles, goals, and acceptance criteria. It includes a requirement reference and is testable. However, it could be improved by adding more specific examples or edge cases for the acceptance criteria.

scores.gpt_judge_rationale: Aligned with REQ-005 and does not invent the separate weekend-prohibition behavior from REQ-004. The acceptance criterion is clear and testable, including timezone/day-boundary cases. Minor refinement: explicitly identify the scheduled timestamp and configured timezone source (and include a boundary example) to remove implementation ambiguity.

story.title: Use cooperative local timezone for weekend migration scheduling
story.i_want: schema migration scheduling to evaluate Saturday and Sunday using the cooperative's configured local timezone
story.so_that: weekend scheduling is determined according to the cooperative's local time
acceptance_criteria: Given a schema migration is scheduled, When the system determines whether its scheduled time falls on Saturday or Sunday, Then it uses the cooperative's configured local timezone to determine the local day of week.

requirements.text: The cooperative's configured local timezone must determine whether a database schema migration is scheduled on Saturday or Sunday.
requirements.quote: Use the cooperative's configured local timezone.
requirements.speaker: Nora (cooperative lead)
requirements.note: The specification does not define any weekend migration restriction or timezone rule for scheduling schema migrations.

scores.judge_rationale: The story has a clear title, actor, intent, and outcome, and the acceptance criteria is testable. However, the requirement is not fully explained, and the note in the requirement indicates that the specification does not define any weekend migration restriction or timezone rule, which suggests the story may be based on an assumption or incomplete context. The acceptance criteria could be more explicit to ensure full testability.

story.title: Display month-by-month reservation count grouped by reservation start month
story.i_want: to see a month-by-month breakdown of reservations in the report, grouped by the start month of each reservation
story.so_that: I can analyze reservation trends over time and make informed decisions
acceptance_criteria: Given the report is generated, when the data is processed, then a table or chart displaying the count of reservations for each month, grouped by the start month of the reservation, is shown
Given the report includes historical data, when the start month is filtered to a specific year, then the reservation count is displayed only for that year
Given the report is viewed by a user with access to the report, when the month-by-month reservation count is requested, then the data is displayed without errors

requirements.text: Add a month-by-month reservation count to the report, grouped by reservation start month.
requirements.quote: Add a month-by-month reservation count to the report, grouped by reservation start month.
requirements.speaker: Nora (cooperative lead)
requirements.note: The requirement is new as HD-REPORTS does not mention adding a month-by-month reservation count to the report.

scores.judge_rationale: The story is well-structured with clear roles, goals, and acceptance criteria. The acceptance criteria are testable and cover key scenarios (displaying data, filtering by year, and ensuring correct display). The requirement is clearly defined and linked. No invented requirements are present.

story.title: Member can save a personal catalogue filter preset with category only
story.i_want: to save a personal catalogue filter preset between visits
story.so_that: I can quickly return to a specific category view without reselecting it each time
acceptance_criteria: Given a member is viewing the catalogue, when they select a category and save the preset, then the preset is saved with only the category information
Given the member returns to the catalogue, when they load the saved preset, then the category is applied but the default alphabetical ordering is preserved

requirements.text: Each member should be able to save one personal catalogue filter preset between visits.
requirements.quote: Let each member save one personal catalogue filter preset between visits.
requirements.speaker: Owen (coordinator)
requirements.note: The specification does not mention allowing members to save personal catalogue filter presets between visits.

requirements.text: The saved preset should only include the category, not the selected dates.
requirements.quote: Save the category, not the selected dates.
requirements.speaker: Owen (coordinator)
requirements.note: The specification does not mention what specific details are saved in a personal catalogue filter preset.

requirements.text: Loading a saved category should not replace the default alphabetical ordering.
requirements.quote: No. Load the saved category when I return, keep alphabetical ordering, and let me clear the preset.
requirements.speaker: Owen (coordinator)
requirements.note: The specification does not mention whether the default alphabetical ordering is preserved when loading a saved category.

scores.judge_rationale: The story has clear user roles, goals, and acceptance criteria, but the requirements are not well-aligned with the story. The acceptance criteria are testable, but the requirement IDs reference requirements that are not clearly defined in the story (they are marked as 'new' and the spec_refs do not provide enough context). Additionally, the story assumes functionality that is not explicitly covered in the specifications, which makes it less testable and potentially reliant on invented requirements.

story.title: Member can clear a saved personal catalogue filter preset
story.i_want: to clear a saved personal catalogue filter preset
story.so_that: I can remove the preset when it is no longer needed
acceptance_criteria: Given a member has a saved preset, when they click the 'clear' control, then the preset is removed from their account

requirements.text: A clear save and clear control should be provided for the preset.
requirements.quote: And do not build a whole design system for the saved preset. A clear save and clear control is enough.
requirements.speaker: Owen (coordinator)
requirements.note: The specification does not mention providing a clear save and clear control for a personal filter preset.

scores.judge_rationale: The story has a clear user persona, goal, and basic acceptance criteria. However, the acceptance criteria are not fully testable as they lack details on how the 'clear' control is implemented or how the removal is verified. Also, the requirement references a quote that may not fully align with the acceptance criteria, and the note indicates a potential discrepancy in the specification. Edits are needed to improve clarity and testability.

human_provenance: Scores 1-10 were adopted by the user after reviewing an AI reviewer's scores and reasons; they are not blind human ratings.
